findings.text: a plan-section-depends-on entry whose section key fails the resource-segment grammar makes section_depends_on return None for the entire mapping, and the roadmap reaches section_dependency_refusals only from _section_scoped_edges (reckon/roadmap.py:557), itself entered only when the mapping is non-empty (reckon/roadmap.py:1924) — so one typo in a section key silently erases every wait in the mapping: the plan reports with no readiness split, the invalid-section-dependency refusal written for exactly this defect (reckon/_schema.py:423-429) cannot fire on an authored plan, and the sections read as declaring no edges at all (probe on the delivered head with a positive control on the same finding channel: a ref naming no target section yields missing-dependency-section, the malformed key yields no section finding).

baseline_suite and after_suite are written as prose, which the store's annotation reads as a bare path naming no file, so annotate_review_of_run resolves no gate log and every read_review caller sees added_failure_count: None for this run even though both logs exist and their set difference is 0 (re-derived here; see gate_log_evidence).

read_plan's deps payload is still built from the whole-plan depends_on meta only, so the goal's read_plan leg is unreachable there at the delivered head — a caller reading read_plan sees no section-scoped dependency and no trace of one, while the mapping surfaces only as roadmap row keys and the ready-set projection; the node records this as a fenced deviation, but the goal sentence it was dispatched with is not met on this leg.
